hook: A lost photographic archive spent 60 years hidden in a foreign attic.

sections.voiceover: A lost photographic archive spent 60 years hidden in a foreign attic.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of old black and white photographs inside a dusty cardboard box.
b_roll: Historical attic interior with dust motes

sections.voiceover: Using a second-hand camera, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler snapped Coventry's bomb sites in 1963. What led the Coventry College of Art student to take those images?
sections.visual_cue: Archival footage of Coventry bomb sites alongside a portrait of Elizabeth Tyler.
b_roll: Coventry post-war bomb sites historical photo
Coventry College of Art exterior archive image

sections.voiceover: Except the archive was moved across four different countries before being rediscovered in an attic.
sections.visual_cue: Map showing the distance from Coventry to Sweden with an overlay of a storage box.
b_roll: Old storage box on a wooden floor

sections.voiceover: Now 80 years old, Elizabeth Tyler sees her archive revealed after 4 countries. Those black and white photographs capture abandoned buildings across Coventry.
sections.visual_cue: Recent photograph of Elizabeth Tyler examining her recovered historical negatives.

sections.voiceover: The collection stayed in Borstahusen, Sweden, for more than 60 years.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the attic space in Sweden where the box was found.
b_roll: Attic window with light streaming through
